title: Pasta Puttanesca
subtitle: Spaghetti with anchovies, capers, and olives
excerpt: Puttanesca is a punchy southern Italian pasta sauce made entirely from pantry staples: anchovies dissolve into the oil to give a deep savoury base, tinned tomatoes provide body, and capers and olives cut through with brine. It comes together in 20 minutes and keeps well in the refrigerator.
sourceNotes: Puttanesca is a robust southern Italian sauce traditionally made with pantry staples. The combination of anchovies, olives, and capers creates an intensely savoury, briny sauce.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the sauce in portions for up to 3 months.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the sauce and freeze half for a quick weeknight meal.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce keeps refrigerated for up to 3 days.

content.text: The anchovies are not there to make the sauce taste fishy: they dissolve completely into the hot oil and become an invisible layer of savouriness underpinning everything else. Do not skip them even if you are not usually an anchovy fan. Capers and black olives are the other two essential ingredients: add 2 tablespoons of drained capers and a handful of pitted black olives with the tomatoes. They are not in the standard ingredient list, but the sauce is incomplete without them. The whole dish should take no longer than the time it takes to boil the pasta.
Bring a large pan of generously salted water to the boil for the pasta. The water should taste pleasantly salty before you add anything to it.

Pour the olive oil into a large frying pan and set it over a medium-low heat. Add the drained anchovies and cook, pressing them down with a wooden spoon, for 2 to 3 minutes until they have dissolved completely into the oil. There should be no visible fish pieces remaining.

Add the sliced garlic and chilli flakes. Cook gently for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until the garlic is soft and fragrant but not coloured. Watch the heat carefully: burnt garlic will make the whole sauce bitter.

Add the tinned tomatoes, breaking them up with a spoon. Add 2 tablespoons of drained capers and a large handful of pitted black olives. Stir to combine and season with black pepper. Hold off on salt until the end: the anchovies, capers, and olives all contribute considerable saltiness.

Simmer the sauce over a medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes until it has thickened and the tomatoes are no longer watery. While it simmers, cook the spaghetti in the boiling water according to packet instructions, removing it 1 minute before the stated time. Reserve a large mug of pasta cooking water before draining.

Drain the spaghetti and add it directly to the sauce in the frying pan. Toss over a medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, adding splashes of pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce and help it coat the strands evenly.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt if needed. Serve immediately. Puttanesca is typically served without cheese: the briny intensity of the sauce is already very full-flavoured.

items.cause: The capers and olives were not drained thoroughly, or extra salt was added before tasting.
items.fix: Do not add any extra salt until the very end, after tasting. Rinse the capers under cold water before using them if they are packed in brine rather than oil.

items.symptom: The garlic tastes bitter and acrid
items.cause: The garlic was cooked over too high a heat and browned before the anchovies had fully dissolved.
items.fix: Keep the heat at medium-low throughout this stage. If the garlic has already caught, start again with a clean pan: there is no fixing burnt garlic once it is in the sauce.

items.symptom: The sauce is too thin and watery
items.cause: The tomatoes were not simmered long enough to reduce, or the lid was left on, trapping steam.
items.fix: Simmer the sauce uncovered over a medium heat for a further 5 to 10 minutes until it reaches a thick, jammy consistency. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon before you add the pasta.
